q1_what_did_you_play: I played Bag of Tricks using its 3-Spark option, then Firework Finale, then Mine Toss, then Spirited Away. This uses all 3 Energy and the available Spark economy, deals the maximum damage I could confidently score from the printed text, and leaves enough Block to fully absorb Nibbit’s telegraphed 12 damage.
q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing Firework Finale first and then Bag of Tricks’ 1-Bomb option, but that line is strictly worse on damage and does not improve survivability. I also considered replacing Spirited Away with Duck and Cover, but that only reduces Block from 12 to 5 with no compensating benefit.
q3_what_it_gave_up: This line gives up the possibility of keeping Firework Finale un-exhausted for a future turn, and it gives up any extra Spark bank that might have been generated if a different bomb-detonation timing were available. It also spends all Energy on damage and Block, leaving no defensive flexibility if the enemy intent were different or if an unexpected extra threat appeared.
q4_different_intent: Yes. If Nibbit had telegraphed a weaker attack, I might have skipped Spirited Away and kept Energy for a different defensive or offensive choice. If it had telegraphed a much larger attack, I would have prioritized Block even more aggressively, possibly choosing Duck and Cover in addition to Spirited Away if Energy allowed, or reconsidering whether to spend Energy on damage at all.
